questions.q: In a Vernier Caliper <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math> divisions of Vernier scale is equal to the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn></math> divisions of main scale. When both jaws of Vernier calipers touch each other, the zero of the Vernier scale is shifted to the left of zero of the main scale and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> Vernier scale division exactly coincides with the main scale reading. One main scale division is equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. While measuring diameter of a spherical body, the body is held between two jaws. It is now observed that zero of the Vernier scale lies between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>31</mn></math> divisions of main scale reading and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>6</mn><mrow><mi>th</mi><mo> </mo></mrow></msup></math> Vernier scale division exactly. coincides with the main scale reading. The diameter of the spherical body will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that 1 M.S.D=1 mm

And 9 M.S.D =10 V.S.D

⇒1 V.S.D=0.9M.S.D=0.9 mm

L.C of vernier caliper =1-0.9=0.1 mm=0.01 cm

Zero error =10-4×0.1 mm=0.6 mm as at zero the, the zero of the vernier is shifted towards left zero error is negative. Therefore, zero error=-0.6 mm.

Reading =M.S.R+V.S.R-  Zero error

Reading=3+6×0.01--0.06

Reading=3+0.06+0.06

Reading=3.12 cm

The closest option is 3.10 cm

questions.q: Identify the physical quantity that cannot be measured using spherometer :
options: Radius of curvature of concave surface
Radius of curvature of convex surface
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A spherometer is a device used for measuring the curvature of surfaces, particularly the radius of curvature of spherical or cylindrical surfaces. It consists of a central leg with a fine screw, and three outer legs that form a tripod. The device is primarily designed for measuring dimensions related to curved surfaces.

Specific rotation is a property related to the rotation of plane-polarized light in a substance. It is not measured using a spherometer. Instead, a polarimeter is typically used to measure specific rotation.

questions.q: Using screw gauge of pitch <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn></math> divisions on its circular scale, the thickness of an object is measured. It should correctly be recorded as,
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Thickness = M.S. Reading + Circular Scale Reading (L.C.)

Here least count is 0.002 cm per division.

From all the four options, the second answer is divisible by this least count. Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.q: A load of mass <math><mi>M</mi><mi> </mi><mi>k</mi><mi>g</mi></math> is suspended from a steel wire of length <math><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></math> and radius <math><mn>1.0</mn><mi> </mi><mi>m</mi><mi>m</mi></math> in Searle's apparatus experiment. The increase in length produced in the wire is <math><mn>4.0</mn><mi> </mi><mi>m</mi><mi>m</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Now the load is fully immersed in a liquid of relative density <math><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo></math> The relative density of the material of load is <math><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo></math> The new value of increase in length of the steel wire is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
δ=ρ0vg×LAy

δ′=ρ0-ρLvg×LAy⇒δ^′δ=ρ0-ρLρ0=8-28

δ′=3 mm

questions.q: The measured value of the length of a simple pendulum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> accuracy. The time for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn></math> oscillations was measured to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn></math> seconds with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> second resolution. From these measurements, the accuracy in the measurement of acceleration due to gravity is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi><mo>%</mo></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Time period of a simple pendulum is given by, T=2πlg.

⇒g=4π2lT2

Therefore, fractional error will be

Δgg=Δll+2ΔTT

=0.220+2140

=1.220

Percentage change =1.220×100=6%

questions.q: In an experiment with vernier callipers of least count <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, when two jaws are joined together the zero of vernier scale lies right to the zero of the main scale and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>6</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> division of vernier scale coincides with the main scale division. While measuring the diameter of a spherical bob, the zero of vernier scale lies in between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> marks and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> division of vernier scale coincides with the main scale division. The diameter of bob is measured as
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The least count is LC=0.1 mm

Zero error (ZE)=6×LC=6×0.1 mm=0.6 mm

The total reading is TR=MSR+VSR×LC-ZE⇒TR=32 mm+(0.1×4) mm-0.6 mm⇒TR=31.8 mm=3.18 cm

questions.q: In a Screw Gauge, fifth division of the circular scale coincides with the reference line when the ratchet is closed. There are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn></math> divisions on the circular scale, and the main scale moves by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> on a complete rotation. For a particular observation the reading on the main scale is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>20</mn><mtext>th </mtext></msup></math> division of the circular scale coincides with reference line. Calculate the true reading.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
L.C. of screw Gauge=0.550=0.01 mm
Zero error of screw Gauge =5×L.C.=5×0.01=0.05 mm
Reading of screw gauge = main scale reading + circular scale reading ×L.C.-Zero error =5+20×0.01-0.05=5.15 mm

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : In a vernier callipers, one vernier scale division is always smaller than one main scale division.
Statement II : The vernier constant is given by one main scale division multiplied by the number of vernier scale divisions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: In general one vernier scale division is smaller than one main scale division but in some modified cases it may be not correct. Also least count is given by one main scale division / number of vernier scale division for normal vernier calliper.

questions.q:
In an experiment to find out the diameter of wire using screw gauge, the following observation were noted:

(a) Screw moves 0.5 mm on main scale in one complete rotation
(b) Total divisions on circular scale =50
(c) Main scale reading is 2.5 mm
(d) 45th  division of circular scale is in the pitch line
(e) Instrument has 0.03 mm negative error Then the diameter of wire is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the data given in the question,

Pitch of the screw gauge=0.5 mm.

Total divisions on the circular scalen=50.

Therefore, the least count of the screw gauge is LC=pitchn=0.550=0.01 mm

Now, MSR=2.5 mm, CSR=45

Diameter reading =MSR+LC×CSR- zero error

⇒d=2.5+0.45--0.03

⇒d=2.98 mm

questions.q: A student measuring the diameter of a pencil of circular cross-section with the help of a vernier scale records the following four readings <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>55</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>34</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>65</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The average of these four reading is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5375</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and the standard deviation of the data is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>07395</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The average diameter of the pencil should therefore be recorded as :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Significant rule says that reading should has same significant figure as that of reading given.

5.5375→ rounded to →5.54.

0.07395→ rounded to→0.07

therefore, 5.54±0.07 mm

questions.q:
Assertion A: If in five complete rotations of the circular scale, the distance travelled on the main scale of the screw gauge is 5 mm and there are 50 total divisions on a circular scale, then the least count is 0.001 cm.

Reason R:
Least Count = Pitch  Total divisions on circular scale 
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is not correct but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is correct.

Both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> are correct and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is the correct explanation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is correct but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is not correct.

Both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> are correct and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is NOT the correct explanation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Ionic bonds are electrostatic forces of attraction that are non-directional in nature.
Thus, (A) is correct. Ionic compounds are soluble in polar solvents that solvate them via ion-dipole interactions.
Thus, $(\mathrm{R})$ is incorrect.

questions.q: For the determination of refractive index of glass slab, a travelling microscope is used whose main scale contains 300 equal divisions equals to 15 cm. The vernier scale attached to the microscope has 25 divisions equals to 24 divisions of main scale. The least count (LC) of the travelling microscope is (in cm) :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & 300 \mathrm{msd}=15 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & 1 \mathrm{msd}=\frac{15}{300} \mathrm{~cm}=0.05 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & 25 \mathrm{vsd}=24 \mathrm{msd} \\ & 1 \mathrm{vsd}=\frac{24}{25} \mathrm{msd} \\ & \mathrm{LC}=1 \mathrm{msd}-1 \mathrm{vsd}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{LC}=1 \mathrm{msd}-\frac{24}{25} \mathrm{msd}=\frac{1}{25} \mathrm{msd} \\ & \mathrm{LC}=\frac{1}{25} \times 0.05=0.002 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}$
correct option (2)

questions.q:
The pitch and the number of divisions, on the circular scale, for a given screw gauge are 0.5 mm and 100 respectively. When the screw gauge is fully tightened without any object, the zero of its circular scale lies 3 divisions below the mean line.

The readings of the main scale and the circular scale, for a thin sheet, are 5.5 mm and 48 respectively, the thickness of this sheet is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
least count =0.5 mm100=0.005 mm

Reading =5.5 mm+48-3×0.005 mm

=5.725 mm.

questions.q:
The vernier scale used for measurement has a positive zero error of 0.2 mm. If while taking a measurement it was noted that 0 on the vernier scale lies between 8.5 cm and 8.6 cm. Vernier coincidence is 6, then the correct value of measurement is cm.

(least count=0.01 cm)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Positive zero error =0.2 mm

Main scale reading =8.5 cm

Vernier scale reading=6×0.01=0.06 cm

Final reading=8.5+0.06-0.02=8.54 cm

questions.q:
A screw gauge of pitch 0.5 mm is used to measure the diameter of uniform wire of length 6.8 cm, the main scale reading is 1.5 mm and circular scale reading is 7. The calculated curved surface area of wire to appropriate significant figures is
[Screw gauge has 50 divisions on the circular scale]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Least Count (L.C)=PN=0.5 mm50=0.01 mm

Length of wire =6.8 cm

Diameter of wire =1.5 mm+7× L.C

=1.5 mm+7×.01=1.57 mm

Curved surface area =πDl

=3.14×6.8×1.57×10-1 cm2

=3.352 cm2=3.4 cm2

questions.q: The diameter of a sphere is measured using a vernier caliper whose 9 divisions of main scale are equal to 10 divisions of vernier scale. The shortest division on the main scale is equal to $1 \mathrm{~mm}$. The main scale reading is $2 \mathrm{~cm}$ and second division of vernier scale coincides with a division on main scale. If mass of the sphere is 8.635 g, the density of the sphere is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given $9 \mathrm{MSD}=10 \mathrm{VSD}\operatorname{mass}=8.635 \mathrm{~g}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{LC}=1 \mathrm{MSD}-1 \mathrm{VSD} \\ & \mathrm{LC}=1 \mathrm{MSD}-\frac{9}{10} \mathrm{MSD} \\ & \mathrm{LC}=\frac{1}{10} \mathrm{MSD} \\ & \mathrm{LC}=0.01 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$ Reading of diameter $=\mathrm{MSR}+\mathrm{LC} \times \mathrm{VSR}\begin{aligned} & =2 \mathrm{~cm}+(0.01) \times(2) \\ & =2.02 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$ Volume of sphere $=\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^3=\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(\frac{2.02}{2}\right)^3=4.32 \mathrm{~cm}^3$ Density $=\frac{\text { mass }}{\text { volume }}=\frac{8.635}{4.32}=1.998 \sim 2.00 \mathrm{~g}$
SECTION -B !

questions.q: The least count of the main scale of a screw gauge is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi> </mi><mi>mm</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The minimum number of divisions on its circular scale required to measure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>μm</mi></math> diameter of a wire is:

questions.solution:

questions.q: The least count of the main scale of a vernier calipers is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. Its vernier scale is divided into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math> divisions and coincide with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn></math> divisions of the main scale. When jaws are touching each other, the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>7</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> division of the vernier scale coincides with a division of the main scale and the zero of vernier scale is lying right side of the zero of the main scale. When this vernier is used to measure the length of the cylinder the zero of the vernier scale between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> VSD coincides with the main scale division. The length of the cylinder is (VSD is vernier scale division)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Zero Error = 0+7×0.1=0.070

Vernier reading = (3.1+4×0.01) –0.07=3.07

questions.q: There are 100 divisions on the circular scale of a screw gauge of pitch $1 \mathrm{~mm}$. With no measuring quantity in between the jaws, the zero of the circular scale lies 5 divisions below the reference line. The diameter of a wire is then measured using this screw gauge. It is found that 4 linear scale divisions are clearly visible while 60 divisions on circular scale coincide with the reference line. The diameter of the wire is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Least count }=\frac{1}{100} \mathrm{~mm}=0.01 \mathrm{~mm} \\ & \text { zero error }=+0.05 \mathrm{~mm} \\ & \text { Reading }=4 \times 1 \mathrm{~mm}+60 \times 0.01 \mathrm{~mm}-0.05 \mathrm{~mm} \\ & =4.55 \mathrm{~mm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: One main scale division of a vernier callipers is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>n</mi><mi>th</mi></msup></math> division of the vernier scale coincide with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi>th</mi></msup></math> division of the main scale. The least count of the callipers in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mm</mi></math> is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
n-1a=na'

a'=n-1an

∴ L.C.=1MSD-1VSD

=a-a' cm

=a-n-1an

=na-na+an=an cm

=10an mm

questions.q: When two resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> connected in series and introduced into the left gap of a meter bridge and a resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is introduced into the right gap, a null point is found at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from left side. When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> are connected in parallel and introduced into the left gap, a resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is introduced into the right-gap to get null point at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from left end. The product of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo> </mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A meter bridge consists of a wire of length 1 m and of uniform cross-sectional area stretched taut and clamped between two thick metallic strips bent at right angles with two gaps across which resistors are to be connected. It works on the principle of the Wheatstone bridge. Therefore, we can write

R1+R210=6040⇒R1+R2=15 Ω

Then for the second case, we can write 

R1R2R1+R2×3=4060⇒R1R2=30 Ω2

questions.q: The diameter of a spherical bob is measured using a vernier callipers. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn></math> divisions of the main scale, in the vernier callipers, are equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math> divisions of vernier scale. One main scale division is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The main scale reading is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>8</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> division of vernier scale was found to coincide exactly with one of the main scale division. If the given vernier callipers has positive zero error of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>04</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo>,</mo></math> then the radius of the bob is _____________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
9 MSD=10 VSD
1 VSD=0.9 mm
1 MSD=1 mm
∴ L.C.=MSD-VSDMSD=1-0.91=0.1
Reading = Main scale reading + L.C. × vernier scale reading
=10+0.1×8
=10.8 mm

Reading of diameter=10.8 mm-0.4 mm=10.4 mm
radius of the bob=5.2 mm
=0.52 cm=52×10-2 cm

questions.q: A student in the laboratory measures thickness of a wire using screw gauge. The readings are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>22</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>23</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>19</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The percentage error is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>121</mn></mfrac><mo>%</mo></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The average value of the readings is xavg=1.19+1.20+1.22+1.234=1.21

Now, absolute error in measurement Δxavg=0.02+0.01+0.01+0.024=0.064=0.015

Percentage error in measurement is =0.0151.21×100%=150121%

So, the value of x=150.

questions.q: A tiny metallic rectangular sheet has length and breadth of 5 mm and 2.5 mm , respectively. Using a specially designed screw gauge which has pitch of 0.75 mm and 15 divisions in the circular scale, you are asked to find the area of the sheet. In this measurement, the maximum fractional error will be $\frac{x}{100}$ where $x$ is _________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Since least count of the instrument can be calculated as $\begin{aligned} & \text { Least count }=\frac{\text { pitch length }}{\text { No. of division on circular scale }} \\ & =\frac{0.75}{15}=0.05 \mathrm{~mm} . \end{aligned}$ Here we are provided $\mathrm{L}=5 \mathrm{~mm} \& \mathrm{~W}=2.5 \mathrm{~mm}\mathrm{L}=5 \mathrm{~mm} \& \mathrm{~W}=2.5 \mathrm{~mm}\because$ We know that $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{L} . \mathrm{W}$ For calculating fractional error, we can write $\frac{\mathrm{dA}}{\mathrm{~A}}=\frac{\mathrm{dL}}{\mathrm{~L}}+\frac{\mathrm{dW}}{\mathrm{~W}}$ Here $\mathrm{dL}=\mathrm{dW}=0.05 \mathrm{~mm}\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{dA}}{\mathrm{~A}}=\frac{0.05}{5}+\frac{0.05}{2.5} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dA}}{\mathrm{~A}}=\frac{1}{100}+\frac{2}{100}=\frac{3}{100} \end{aligned}$ So, $x=3$
